title: Banking
description: Proactive loan offer, finding documents (transactions with receipts) and password reset by phone. Italian customers.
notes:
Two use cases on one customer base.

1) Proactive loan offer: the assistant spots customers whose 3-month average balance is below 300 EUR (rule R-LOWBAL) and offers a personal loan of 5,000-10,000 EUR over 24 or 36 months at 6% APR. Elena Bianchi (C001, +39 347 000 0301) is the main case: average 212.40 EUR, eligible up to 10,000 EUR, prefers phone. Chiara Esposito (C003) and Francesca Romano (C005) are below the threshold but must NOT get an offer (identity check pending / existing loan). Alessandro Conti (C004) is just above the threshold. Marco Rossi (C002) is healthy and has an example loan request.

2) Finding documents: every transaction carries its own receipt (doc_id, doc_category, doc_title, doc_url). Rule R-DOCLINKS: up to 5 links go into the chat; above that the assistant sends the customer's documents_page_url. 29 transactions, built to test how many results come back:
- 1 result: Alessandro, the notary last month (Studio Notarile Bruno); Marco, the car deposit last month (Autosalone Bellini).
- 2 to 5 results: Alessandro, the electrician last month: 3 transfers, 1,200 EUR in total. A 4th, made today (pending), must not count as last month.
- more than 5 results: Alessandro, 7 renovation transfers last year; Elena, rent: one payment a month for 8 months (the 3 most recent give 3 results, all of them 8).
- older than 6 months: Alessandro's renovation (last year) and F24 / insurance; Elena's rent 7 and 8 months ago; Marco's tuition 9 months ago.
Messy payee names on purpose: 'G. Ferrari' and 'Ferari Giorgio' (the electrician), 'VITALE MARCO PIASTRELLE' and 'M. Vitale', 'Costa Ed. Srl', 'Greco P. Idraulica', 'Tinteggiature Rosi'; no name at all (only in the causale): the window fitter 'Serramenti Torino snc' and one rent payment ('Imm. Duomo'); 'IMMOB. DUOMO SRL' and 'Immobiliare Duomo' for the landlord. The beneficiary IBAN stays the same, so it can identify the payee when the name does not. Dates are relative to the day the dataset is loaded, so reload it to keep 'last month' and 'last year' true.

3) Password reset by phone (conversational IVR). The caller is recognised by the phone number (customers.phone); customers.online_banking.password_status says whether the password is blocked. Security interview (rule R-IDENTITY): ID card number, last three digits of the current account (the IBAN in accounts), tax code. ID card and tax code are stored MASKED (* = hidden character: the full values are never kept), so compare the visible characters only. If the interview is passed: case 3A hands the call to an operator with a note, case 3B asks the backend for the reset and gets OK or KO (rule R-PWRESET, history in password_requests, interviews in identity_checks). Test customers:
- Marco Rossi (C002, +39 333 000 0302): blocked, no history: the clean case. 3A or 3B ends in OK.
- Chiara Esposito (C003, +39 349 000 0303): blocked, but three failed interviews today (max 3 a day) and KYC still pending: no self-service, hand over to an operator. A reset yesterday was refused (KYC_PENDING).
- Alessandro Conti (C004, +39 335 000 0304): blocked; passed the interview this morning and already got a temporary password (PR6002): a new request is refused (KO, ALREADY_REQUESTED).
- Elena Bianchi (C001) and Francesca Romano (C005): password active, nothing to reset (Francesca had a reset 62 days ago).

4) Several customer matches. Elena Bianchi (C001, +39 347 000 0301, Milano, born 14 February 1984) and Elena Maria Bianchi (C006, +39 345 000 0306, Bergamo, born 5 September 1979) share a first and a last name. A search for "Elena" or "Bianchi" matches both, so the assistant has to ask which one; "Elena Bianchi" is an exact match for C001, "Elena Maria" finds only C006. Phone number or date of birth tells them apart. C006 has a healthy balance and is not part of the other use cases.

5) Low-balance alerts (operator demo in Teneo, solution MCP Demo: flow "low balance alerts"). For the demo the seed data holds ONLY Chiara Esposito's alert (AL4002). The alerts of Elena Bianchi (A1001, 212.40 EUR) and Francesca Romano (A1005, 120.00 EUR) are left out on purpose: the flow lists the accounts with an average balance below 300 EUR, adds the missing alerts with set_collection (the existing one is kept) and, at the end, clears the whole alerts collection. Reset database brings the single seed alert back. Until the alerts are created again, the proactive loan call for Elena Bianchi has no open alert to hand it over.
